title: Wrap a character
content:
Hey, i am trying to wrap a character fully like a mummy, what would be the best way to do that in MD ?

![31e4c23b0a59458d99bd33ecc407304f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/06b2a4ce6cdf41f6803c8e9beadd9d18/images/31e4c23b0a59458d99bd33ecc407304ftelegram-cloud-photo-size-4-5974463680022169473-y.jpg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hey! Well, it really depends on whether it's going to be a mummy-style wrapping, wrapping like a plastic bag, or another way of compressing material inside. As the reference from the image you shared is not clear.For a "mummy" kind of wrapping, you can always create a 3D line over the avatar to set the starting point and sew an edge to that line. You can play either with one pattern for the whole character or by creating the start and end points for each piece. However, this last method will be time-consuming. Using Pins (Box) will help locate the different parts around conflicting areas, similar to creating a knot.
content_description: Discover effective techniques for fully wrapping a character like a mummy in your MD projects.

title: Can not perform keycombo to call transform dialog Wacom tablet
content:
I'm seeing an issue with a Wacom tablet and not being able to perform Lmb + drag > rmb. With a wacom tablet, also not with a magic mouse. PS with magic mouse you cant left click, drag then do rigghtclick. Whoever ever made this button combo did not even test it. Its impossible with a MagicMouse because its one big button

Same issue is for WacomTablet. Also trackpad.

All those hotkeys are not functioning properly. Seen in older versions of MD and its stilll there.

When a use does LMB drag move, then rightclick. According to manual and videos, a dialog should show "Move Distance", when doing scalling, "Transform" dialog should show. But with all my devices, i simply get the regular rightclick context menu. No other dialog appears

As an extra notion. Why isn't there simply a transform function in the context menu, why does it need this weird keycombo? Same goes for move, alsondorsnt work.

I've made screen grabs of the behavior. Will add them tomorrow

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hey! There is an old post that might help you out with this issue.Using the F1 key might solve the issue while working with Tablet.https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/c53f3c6078904a9dbe7a57e1d115f09f the Move Distance tool, the 'Moving Distance' is based on the line differences between the start point and moving points.  Without a moving point or segment, the program can't calculate the distance and directions.

title: Blending 3D into 2D: Unveiling the Concept Art of “The Scent”
content:
## _Concept artist Rui Li shares how 3D tool like Marvelous Designer enhances 2D illustration, shaping the intricate world of his concept art - The Scent. From hyper-realistic fabrics to immersive storytelling, discover how 3D-assisted costume design improves efficiency, detail, and creative flexibility._

* * *

![0214c9e458e4433a8cae6fb57638f2fa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/0214c9e458e4433a8cae6fb57638f2fa%E6%9D%8E%E7%9D%BF-%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%90%88%E9%9B%86gif.gif)

# **Interview with**[**Rui Li**](https://www.artstation.com/melodyoflost)**| The Scent | Concept Artist & Illustrator**

* * *

# **Please introduce yourself to the Marvelous Designer community.**

Hello everyone, my name is Rui. I am a concept artist and illustrator from China. My primary work involves creating concept designs and promotional illustrations for games. I have been in this industry for 15 years and started incorporating 3D software into my workflow about 5-6 years ago to enhance my creative process.

# **What led you to concept art and character design? Were there any artists or works that inspired you?**

After graduating, I went straight into the game industry as a concept artist. I’ve drawn inspiration from many different artists over the years, but there isn’t one particular artist who had a defining influence on me. Since I’ve worked on a variety of projects with different styles, I’ve found new inspirations at every stage of my career. Early on, I was greatly influenced by **Craig Mullins** while working on realistic projects. Growing up, I played a lot of Japanese games and watched anime and manga, which also left a deep impression on me. Artists like **Katsuya Terada** , **Yoshitaka Amano** , and manga creators like **Takehiko Inoue** and **Rumiko Takahashi** have all influenced my artistic style. My taste is quite eclectic.

![5d482a5942694df688af72b5aa16cb78](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/5d482a5942694df688af72b5aa16cb78CM%20%E4%BD%9C%E5%93%81%E5%90%88%E9%9B%86gif.gif)

Artist: Craig Mullins

![106aa07a17e94d84a2283f8feab0dbd0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/106aa07a17e94d84a2283f8feab0dbd0%E5%AF%BA%E7%94%B0%E5%85%8B%E4%B9%9F1.jpg)

Artist: Katsuya Terada

![69eb7e606698484d9524936f2981fd8b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/69eb7e606698484d9524936f2981fd8b%E5%A4%A9%E9%87%8E%E5%96%9C%E5%AD%9D1.jpg)

Artist: Yoshitaka Amano

# **Your worldbuilding for _The Scent_ is fascinating! What inspired it, and how would you describe its setting and artistic vision?**

A few years ago, I became passionate about collecting perfumes and exploring different scents. Last year, I finally had some free time and decided to build a world around the theme of “fragrance.” Over time, as I continued creating, the story naturally evolved and became more refined.

![118da70db2364902a28ac039b74f76a3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/118da70db2364902a28ac039b74f76a3final-22%20%281%29.jpg)

The story revolves around a perfumer who uses scents to heal emotional wounds. Each character embodies a unique fragrance, representing a particular emotion. Visually, I wanted to create a sense of vintage opulence. The aesthetic is inspired by the late 19th century, a period that blends the elegance of Art Nouveau with the structured forms of Art Deco. Since different fragrances originate from various places, the design incorporates diverse cultural influences, making for a richly layered visual experience.

![0725a55152a44170bb18cacdbad06a11](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/0725a55152a44170bb18cacdbad06a11final.jpg)

# **What software and tools do you mainly use in your workflow?**

I primarily work with **Blender, Daz Studio, Marvelous Designer, and Photoshop**.

# **Your creative process is based on 3D modeling before bringing the work into Photoshop for painting. What led you to adopt this workflow?**

I initially adopted this workflow to improve efficiency and image quality. Over time, I’ve realized that 3D-assisted illustration brings several key benefits:

  1. **Faster workflow** – In commercial projects, recurring characters and props can be reused across different scenes, making the process much more efficient.

  2. **Better realism** – 3D rendering provides accurate lighting, depth, material reflections, and textures that would be difficult to replicate with pure hand-drawing.

  3. **More flexibility** – With 3D, I can adjust camera angles and lighting at any stage. In contrast, 2D workflows tend to be more linear—once the composition, lighting, and colors are set, making big changes later is often impractical.


![04c0bb2494164f55b72d2b0936b8f1df](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/04c0bb2494164f55b72d2b0936b8f1dfimg_v3_02k1_df28d569-496c-4603-8f07-7251f105c8cg.jpg)![2ef8a55081fd42bd968205172726b3d1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/2ef8a55081fd42bd968205172726b3d1img_v3_02k1_599edcff-2748-4e3d-afec-761d9888479g.jpg)

# **When designing character garments in Marvelous Designer, which aspects or features do you focus on the most?**

I primarily focus on **accurate fabric simulation** , which is why I mainly use the **2D pattern-making tools** and **basic animation features** to refine my designs.

# **Could you share a specific example of how Marvelous Designer played a key role in your creative process?**

In _The Mastic_ , about **one-quarter of the scene is dedicated to fabric details** , which play a crucial role in enhancing the composition. The folds and drapery not only complement the character but also help **fill the scene naturally** , creating a richer and more immersive atmosphere.

Marvelous Designer’s ability to generate **realistic fabric textures and movement** brings an added level of authenticity to my work. It also **softens the stiffness** that can sometimes come with 3D-assisted creations. I see it as a **visual and compositional mediator** , seamlessly blending characters with their surroundings. The way fabric interacts with objects in the scene further enhances the character’s presence, making the world feel more alive.

![e4670ac912164810af9ab1ca607aef7f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/e4670ac912164810af9ab1ca607aef7fRuxiang3.jpg)![85f534f6839b44728e97cbdde0d20039](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/85f534f6839b44728e97cbdde0d20039img_v3_02k1_835cfbe5-e3ad-4760-982d-27b073a2aaeg.jpg)

# **Any practical tips for artists looking to use Marvelous Designer for concept character costume design?**

The best advice? Start using it right away. Marvelous Designer’s pattern-based approach helps artists understand how clothing actually fits and moves, which is essential for making designs more believable.

That said, don’t rely entirely on raw 3D outputs—while simulations provide a strong foundation, they often need additional refinement. Shapes may lack structural clarity, so post-processing is key to achieving a polished final design.

![76a524a2ed044fb798d14a7d5acab3b1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/dded25398da64f8c8e439e848cba06b9/images/76a524a2ed044fb798d14a7d5acab3b1%E8%95%BE%E5%A7%86.png)

title: Long Collar Midi Shoulder Pad Dress
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/98d61e3616b5432e9d0a797d16e483c6/images/7333183758f341a69b2216d0a4fc02baLong%20Collar%20Midi%20Shoulder%20Pad%20Dress_Pose%20.jpg)

* * *

This dress is a sophisticated, vintage-inspired long-sleeve midi dress in a vibrant turquoise shade. It features structured shoulder pads, giving it a bold, powerful silhouette reminiscent of classic tailored designs. The collar is elongated and tied into a soft bow, with a keyhole cutout just beneath for a subtle touch of elegance. The bodice is fitted with decorative stitching and button detailing running down the center, enhancing the waistline. The skirt flares out gently from the waist, creating a flowy, graceful look. This style combines vintage charm with a modern, polished vibe — perfect for formal gatherings or a statement work outfit.
content_description: Discover a stunning vintage-inspired turquoise midi dress that blends classic elegance with modern sophistication, perfect for making a statement at any formal occasion.
